acceptance.output_evidence: The reading is delivered in the record and is NOT self-graded. (a) SHOULD IT BE RETIRED AT ALL: on the vocabulary axis, YES -- STORED_IN restates a fact the graph already holds (CG-s-32: 135 of 135 source keys carry an OWNED_BY edge naming the same bucket; independently, 232 S3Key -OWNED_BY-> S3_BUCKET edges exist), and a term that adds no fact is a maintenance cost with no return. But the vocabulary axis is not the only axis, and this cell's finding is that the PRODUCER axis disagrees with it: RETIRE-BY-DELETE and RETIRE-BY-RE-POINT look identical from the vocabulary's side and are opposite acts from the producer's, because STORED_IN's sole-writer property is load-bearing for derive_stitch's re-entrancy and OWNED_BY has no such property. THE RULING AUTHORIZED THE UNSAFE ONE, and nothing in either order's criteria could have caught that, because the coupling lives between two separately-graded orders. So: retire it, but by DELETING the emit, and only after the drop-on-read gets a provenance mark instead of a type test. (b) SEMANTIC BAR OR NAMING PROBLEM: it is BOTH, and collapsing them is the error. It is not merely a naming problem, because OWNED_BY is ALREADY overloaded before STORED_IN arrives -- cse_schema.py:323 maps it to OWNS (governance) while cse_emit_graphhead.py:125-127 maps the SAME edge to CONTAINS when the destination is a bucket, and two rollup seams traverse it as containment. A term that already means two things under one name is not a term another term can be folded into; folding location in would make it three. But it is ALSO not an irreducible semantic bar, because a third term resolves it cleanly: a distinct LOCATED_IN or CONTAINED_BY would let STORED_IN retire into a term that means location and leave OWNS to mean custody, which is what the three containment readers actually want. That is a schema act under Rule 24's four postulates with a word-boundary token census, and it is deliberately NOT taken here -- minting vocabulary to satisfy a retirement is the same circularity as editing the three readers to satisfy the condition that measures them. (c) HOW TO CENSUS A RETIREMENT BY CONSTRUCTION: the estate's defect is not that anyone reasoned badly -- condition 1 was written BY the seat enforcing the anti-scoped-domain rule, and it specified a scoped domain, which is how strong the pull is. THREE THINGS WOULD FIX IT MECHANICALLY. (i) THE AMENDMENT THIS CELL LANDED: the manifest now says on its own face that it is an unsound denominator for a retirement question and names the unscoped sweep as the required second arm -- prose, but prose sitting exactly where the next agent will be standing. (ii) A RETIREMENT'S ACCEPT SHOULD REQUIRE A PRINTED DELTA BETWEEN TWO DENOMINATORS, never a single count. This order did that and it is why the finding is legible; generalised, no retirement criterion should be satisfiable by one number, because one number cannot show that its domain was wrong. (iii) AND THE ONE THIS ROUND ADDS, which no existing rule requires: A RETIREMENT MUST PRINT THE WRITER COUNT OF THE SURVIVING TERM BESIDE THE READER CENSUS. This project has now been surprised twice by the same shape -- once on readers (W1-S38) and once on writers (W1-S47) -- and both times the missing number was one a script could have printed in a second. A reader census asks whether anything breaks when the term disappears; a writer census asks whether anything breaks when the SURVIVOR is asked to carry more, and only the second can see a re-point that poisons a producer's own re-entrancy.

mutant.description: FIVE ARMS, each able to make its criterion read the other way, and none of them stored -- every one is re-derived in the run that reports it. (a) THE TREE ARM: h1_tree_control.marker exists ONLY on branch wk-cldgrph-8-1, and TREE_POSITIVE_CONTROL fires only if BOTH the native git enumeration and the comp-rail return it. Had the rail resolved its corpus root to the MAIN tree -- the exact pre-fix hazard, which returns a well-formed zero with a real denominator and names no tree -- the marker would be absent and the arm would read NOT-FIRED. This is the arm that makes every other denominator in this instance admissible from a linked worktree. (b) THE CLASSIFIER ARM: one planted line per class through the same classifier the census uses; a classifier that collapsed FIXTURE into PROSE would drop three real consumers and print 3 of 4. (c) THE SUBSTRING ARM: STORED_INLINE_POLICIES must NOT be counted -- a bare substring sweep returns hundreds of hits in this repository, most of them that token, and the word boundary is the whole difference between a census and a number. (d) THE FALSIFIER ARM, WHICH IS THE ONLY TWO-SIDED ONE: the verdict function is run on a population wholly held by its domain (must return VALID) AND on the same population with one member outside (must return VOID). A falsifier that can only ever return today's answer is a promise, not a control, so both branches are exercised inside the run. (e) THE EGRESS ARM: five planted positives, one per forbidden act family, through the SAME patterns as the real sweep -- because a detector that cannot go non-zero on the positive case is a constant wearing a measurement's clothes, and five zeros from such a detector would be indistinguishable from five zeros from a working one. AND ONE SELF-DIRECTED CONTROL WORTH NAMING SEPARATELY: the egress detector is INSIDE its own swept denominator rather than excluded from it, with its patterns and plant assembled from fragments so the literals never appear as text -- a verifier scoped by the same set as the act cannot see an omission, and excluding itself is exactly that scoping.
